note: Reviewed CDB90 match 150, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Soublette’s report dated 8 August 1819 describes the 7 August engagement of Bolívar’s Liberating Army and Barreiro’s royalist field army at Boyacá. Its reported 13 killed plus 53 wounded also explains why the CDB 66 is casualties, not deaths. Preserve the CDB estimate as one local force per side, with no nationality subdivision or modern Colombian army identity. These sources review event and force identity; CDB numerical estimates and uncertainty are retained, not independently certified. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name PATRIOT ARMY): Sources identify this local battlefield force. The display name clarifies the original CDB designation; its numerical estimates and uncertainty are unchanged. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name SP ARMY): Sources identify this local battlefield force. The display name clarifies the original CDB designation; its numerical estimates and uncertainty are unchanged.
